run.question: I have a slow query on the 'app-191-profile' index. Use the profile option to analyze this query and tell me the query type used: {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}}

report.summary: The exact index named, app-191-profile, exists on the registered Elasticsearch target (health green, status open, 6 documents, 7.1kb) and maps message as text, status as keyword and timestamp as date. Running the submitted query with profile enabled (time_field=timestamp, since @timestamp is not mapped and the window filter cannot be disabled) returned 3 documents and a profile whose query tree shows the wildcard query executed as a type "MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper" with description "message:*timeout*", nested inside a type "ConstantScoreQuery" over a "BooleanQuery" that also holds the timestamp range as an "IndexOrDocValuesQuery". So the query type used is a wildcard query, executed through the constant-score blended multi-term rewrite. The single profiled execution was fast, not slow: took 35 ms end-to-end, query phase 2,191,833 ns (~2.19 ms) on 1 of 1 shard successful, timed_out false; the 'slow query' premise is not supported by this execution, and with no baseline I make no claim about any latency trend. A leading-wildcard term-dictionary scan is the plausible cost driver at larger term cardinality, but with 6 documents it is a hypothesis, not an observed problem.

claims.text: The index app-191-profile exists on target m0-otel-20260909 (source otel-demo) with health green, status open, docs.count 6 and store.size 7.1kb.
The mapping of app-191-profile is: message type text, status type keyword, timestamp type date. There is no @timestamp field, so a time_field must be supplied for any search on this index.

The profile of the submitted query {"wildcard": {"message": "*timeout*"}} shows the wildcard clause executed as type "MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper" with description "message:*timeout*", as a child of a type "BooleanQuery" (description "#message:*timeout* #IndexOrDocValuesQuery(indexQuery=timestamp:[1795256683000 TO 1795343083999], ...)") that in turn is wrapped by a type "ConstantScoreQuery" (the injected time filter on timestamp). The wildcard's own timings were create_weight 11722 ns, build_scorer 396757 ns, next_doc 8875 ns over 4 calls, totaling 419668 ns.

The profiled search matched 3 documents in the queried window (total 3, relation eq), returned with timestamps 2026-11-22T10:19:00Z, 2026-11-22T10:21:00Z and 2026-11-22T10:23:00Z and messages 'Request timeout after 30 seconds', 'Database query timeout exceeded limit' and 'Socket timeout during file upload', all status error. Shards: 1 total, 1 successful, 0 failed, 0 skipped; timed_out false; top-level took 35 ms; query phase 2,191,833 ns; top-level ConstantScoreQuery 2,191,833 ns.

The profile's query array contains a second, separate entry of type "TermQuery" with description "message:timeout" (next_doc_count 4, time_in_nanos 130396) alongside the ConstantScoreQuery that carries the wildcard and the timestamp filter; the request submitted contains only the wildcard clause, so the origin of this TermQuery entry is not explained by the request.

Against the 'slow query' premise for this execution: the profiled run completed in 35 ms took with a 2.19 ms query phase over a 6-document index, timed_out false, no failed shards. This is one execution only and no latency baseline was supplied or fetched, so no trend or comparison is claimed.

The structural cost risk of this query is the leading wildcard on the analyzed text field message: the rewrite to "MultiTermQueryConstantScoreBlendedWrapper" cannot seek an index-term prefix and must walk the term dictionary, so cost scales with distinct terms rather than document count. At the observed 6 documents the profile shows no such cost (sub-millisecond wildcard timings), so this remains a scaling hypothesis, not an observed cause.

gaps: No latency baseline or historical search-latency series for app-191-profile was supplied or retrieved, so the claim that the query is 'slow' is unchecked; only the single profiled execution at 2026-11-22T10:24:53Z (took 35 ms) is observed.
Search slow logs and per-query history in Elasticsearch were not inspected; the profile tool view covers one execution and one shard.
The origin and purpose of the separate "TermQuery" description "message:timeout" entry in the profile's query array is unknown; it does not appear in the submitted request body.
The index reports 6 total documents while 3 matched the wildcard inside the queried window; the content and timestamps of the remaining documents were not read, so their relevance is unknown.
A first search attempt without a time_field returned INVALID_PARAMS (TIME_FIELD_REQUIRED: index maps timestamp, not @timestamp); that failed view has no citable evidence and produced no results.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so any index/settings change history could not be checked.
next_steps: If the 'slow query' report refers to a different window or cluster, collect Elasticsearch slow-log entries or repeated profiled executions (with percentiles of took) for app-191-profile to establish a baseline before judging latency.

Consider replacing the leading wildcard on the text field message with an analyzed/n-gram or keyword-normalized field, or query_string with a prefix-capable term, if term-dictionary walking becomes costly at larger scale.
Confirm whether any client or intermediary adds the extra message:timeout TermQuery to this request, since its source is unexplained by the submitted body.
